# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 17 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 17

**17:1** A decree went out from King Augustus that all those in Bethlehem of Judea should register for the census. Joseph said to himself: "I will register my sons, but what shall I do about this child? How shall I register her? As my wife? I am too ashamed. As my daughter? But all the children of Israel know she is not my daughter. The day of the Lord will determine this, as the Lord wills."

**17:2** He saddled the donkey and put Mary on it. His son led the donkey by the head, and Joseph walked behind. When they had come within three miles, Joseph glanced back and saw that Mary looked sad. He thought to himself: "Perhaps what is inside her is causing her distress." He looked back again and this time saw her laughing. He called to her: "Mary, what is the matter with you? A moment ago your face was sad, and now you are laughing."

**17:3** She replied: "It is because I see two peoples with my eyes: one weeping and mourning, and the other rejoicing and exulting."

**17:4** When they had reached the midpoint of the road, Mary said: "Help me down from the donkey. The child inside me is pressing to come out." He helped her down and said: "Where can I take you to shelter you? This place is desolate."
